Race is a huge part of identity but it's not totally self-administered. Most people are socially assigned race based mostly on their appearance. The only difference scientifically in skin color is melanin, but it has historically been used for much more nefarious reasons. But there have been major flaws with race-based medical care. People from certain continental backgrounds in particular have had issues because of how many ethnicities there are in that broad category. For example, some groups have the lowest rates of obesity and obesity related diseases. Some subgroups are on whole social-economically better off than others, and therefore they have significantly lower rates of obesity, heart disease and diabetes. In fact, some specific immigrant groups have higher rates of those diseases than black or Latinos in the US. Because the largest groups in the US are from one specific background, race actually has a negative effect medically on these smaller groups because their medical treatment differs from groups that have significantly higher amounts of capital on whole. Much of the science behind medically treating race is about ethnicity/culture, basing treatment off diet, socioeconomic status and medical sensitivities. We do classify race based on skin color but very loosely. In fact, even the racist scientists in the 1900's determined skin color was not a determining factor in determining someone's race for citizenship. In fact, one of the cases literally changed the definitions of white to include people from a specific region, who traditionally were considered from another continent because of dark skin, because a man argued in the courts that he was from the same geographical region as a religious figure. We see the same with groups from certain European countries getting considered white and groups from other regions flip flopping between white and Asian.

Race tells us to view human differences and determines societal definitions from them. Continental background is not genetically passed down, but what we consider traits associated with that background are. Parents from that background have certain physical features so plugged into a punnet square those features will be passed down too. But if the parent moves to the US, what isn't passed down to that child is the culture, languages, etc. Those are learned behaviors. Now back on the controversial symbol being used as a symbol: socially, we look at certain physical features and we determine those features mean the person is from that background. More deeply, we then associate the meanings behind how people from that background are viewed socially.
